summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -4 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.4%; weakest: Lean hogs -17.5%. Key releases ahead: US Core CPI m/m (11-10 8:30 AM ET); US CPI m/m (11-10 8:30 AM ET); US Core PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET); US PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.88% (-36 bp in a month), 2-year 4.56% (-24 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (-12 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.04% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.73 (-0.5% in a month, +3.5% YTD). USD/BRL 5.507 (+9.7% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.659 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.50 (+1.7%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -3.3% in a month (+10.3% YTD); VIX 20.0. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 85.69 $/bbl (-5.8% in a month), Brent 91.02, ULSD 4.089 $/gal (-10.9%), natural gas 3.27 (-7.8%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -5.7% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.9%, Hang Seng +1.4%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -7.3% in a month; gold -3.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
